translations.literal: Bureau of Military Affairs; Bureau of Palace Attendants; Commissioner of the Three Commissions; Hanlin Academy; Readers-in-Waiting and Lecturers-in-Waiting; Lecturer at the Hall for Veneration of Governance; Academicians of the Various Halls; Academicians of the Various Pavilions; Various Compiler and Direct Attendant posts; Eastern Palace offices; Princely Establishment offices
translations.idiomatic: Bureau of Military Affairs; Bureau of Palace Attendants; Commissioner of the Three Commissions; Hanlin Academy; Readers-in-Waiting and Lecturers-in-Waiting; Lecturer at the Hall for Veneration of Governance; Academicians of the Various Halls; Academicians of the Various Pavilions; Various Compiler and Direct Attendant posts; Eastern Palace offices; Princely Establishment offices

sentences.zh: 樞密院

translations.literal: Bureau of Military Affairs
translations.idiomatic: Bureau of Military Affairs

sentences.zh: 掌軍國機務、兵防、邊備、戎馬之政令，出納密命，以佐邦治。

translations.literal: It administers state military affairs, defense of troops, frontier preparedness, and policies concerning horses and military mounts; it receives and issues secret orders to assist in governing the realm.
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw state military affairs, troop defense, frontier preparedness, and policies on warhorses and mounts, receiving and issuing secret orders to assist in governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 凡侍衛諸班直、內外禁 兵招募、閱試、遷補、屯戍、賞罰之事，皆掌之。

translations.literal: All matters of recruitment, examination, promotion and reassignment, garrison deployment, and rewards and punishments for the various guard shifts of the Imperial Bodyguard and for inner and outer forbidden troops were under its charge.
translations.idiomatic: It handled recruitment, examinations, promotions, reassignments, garrison duty, and rewards and punishments for every guard shift of the Imperial Bodyguard and for all inner and outer forbidden troops.

sentences.zh: 以升揀、廢置揭帖兵籍；

translations.literal: It used promotion and selection, abolition and establishment, and posted registers of military rolls;
translations.idiomatic: It promoted and selected personnel, abolished or established posts, and maintained posted registers of military rolls;

sentences.zh: 有調發更戍 ，則遣使給降兵符。

translations.literal: when there was mobilization for rotation of garrisons, it dispatched envoys to issue military tallies.
translations.idiomatic: when troops were mobilized for rotational garrison duty, it sent envoys to issue military tallies.

sentences.zh: 除授內侍省官及武選官，將領路分都監、緣邊都巡檢使以上。

translations.literal: It appointed officials of the Directorate of Palace Attendants and military-selection officials, and commanders at the circuit level and above such as regional supervisors and frontier chief inspection commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: It appointed officials of the Directorate of Palace Attendants and military-selection officials, along with circuit-level commanders and above—regional supervisors, frontier chief inspection commissioners, and the like.

sentences.zh: 大事 則稟奏，其付授者用宣；

translations.literal: Major affairs were reported to the throne for decision; those entrusted for execution used proclamations (xuan);
translations.idiomatic: Major matters were reported to the throne; assignments for their execution used proclamations (xuan);

sentences.zh: 小事則擬進，其付授者用劄。

translations.literal: minor affairs were drafted for submission; those entrusted for execution used documents (zha).
translations.idiomatic: Minor matters were drafted for submission; assignments for their execution used documents (zha).

sentences.zh: 先具所得旨，關門下省審覆。

translations.literal: It first set forth the received imperial intent and submitted it to the Chancellery for review.
translations.idiomatic: It first recorded the received imperial intent and referred the matter to the Chancellery for review.

sentences.zh: 面 得旨者為錄白，批奏得畫者為畫旨，並留為底。

translations.literal: Those who received the intent in audience were recorded as "recorded white"; those approved in memorial with the imperial brush were "drawn intent"; both were retained as copies on file.
translations.idiomatic: Intent received in audience was recorded as "recorded white"; memorials approved with the imperial brush were "drawn intent"; both were kept on file as master copies.

sentences.zh: 惟以白紙錄送，皆候報施行。

translations.literal: Only plain paper records were sent; all awaited report before implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Only plain-paper records were forwarded; nothing took effect until confirmation was reported back.

sentences.zh: 其被御寶 批旨者，即送門下省繳覆。

translations.literal: Those bearing the imperial seal and brush approval were at once sent to the Chancellery for surrender and review.
translations.idiomatic: Documents bearing the imperial seal and brush approval were sent immediately to the Chancellery for surrender and review.

sentences.zh: 應給誥者，關中書省命詞。

translations.literal: When patent letters of appointment were to be issued, the Secretariat was notified to draft the commission text.
translations.idiomatic: When formal letters of appointment were required, the Secretariat was asked to draft the commission text.

sentences.zh: 即事幹大計，造作、支移軍器， 及除都副承旨、三衙管軍、三路沿邊帥臣、太僕寺官，文臣換右職，仍同三省取旨。

translations.literal: Matters touching major policy, manufacture and transfer of military equipment, and appointments of chief and deputy chief secretaries, commanders of the Three Commands, frontier commanders of the three circuits, Director of the Imperial Stud officials, and civil officials transferred to military rank still required joint decision with the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Matters touching major policy, the manufacture and transfer of military equipment, and appointments of chief and deputy chief secretaries, commanders of the Three Commands, frontier commanders on the three circuits, Director of the Imperial Stud officials, or civil officials moved to military rank still required joint approval with the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 宋初，循唐、五代之制，置樞密院，與中書對持文武二柄，號為「二府」。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, following Tang and Five Dynasties institutions, the Bureau of Military Affairs was established; with the Secretariat it held the two handles of civil and military power, styled the "Two Offices."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, following Tang and Five Dynasties practice, the Bureau of Military Affairs was established. Together with the Secretariat it held the civil and military handles of power, known as the "Two Offices."

sentences.zh: 院在中書之 北，印有「東院」、「西院」之文，共為一院，但行東院印。

translations.literal: The bureau lay north of the Secretariat; its seal bore the words "Eastern Office" and "Western Office"—one bureau in all, but only the Eastern Office seal was used.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau stood north of the Secretariat. Its seal bore "Eastern Office" and "Western Office," though it was a single bureau; only the Eastern Office seal was used in practice.

sentences.zh: 而職事條目頗多。

translations.literal: Yet the entries of official duties were quite numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Its roster of duties was nevertheless extensive.

sentences.zh: 神宗初 政，迺省其務之細者歸之有司，而增置審官西院，專領閤門祗候以上至諸司使差遣。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Shenzong's reign, minor tasks were cut back and returned to the relevant offices; the Western Office for Review of Appointments was added, specializing in assignments from Gatehouse ushers upward to bureau commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong first took power, minor tasks were trimmed and returned to the proper offices, while the Western Office for Review of Appointments was added to handle assignments from Gatehouse ushers up through bureau commissioners.

sentences.zh: 官 制行，隨事分隸六曹，專以本兵為職，而國信、民兵、牧馬總領，仍舊隸焉。

translations.literal: When the new official system took effect, duties were divided among the Six Ministries as appropriate; the bureau was devoted chiefly to core military affairs, while overall charge of diplomatic credentials, militia, and horse husbandry still remained subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: Under the new official system, duties were parceled out to the Six Ministries as appropriate; the bureau focused on core military affairs, while overall charge of diplomatic credentials, militia, and horse husbandry remained under it.

sentences.zh: 舊分四房 ，曰兵，曰吏，曰戶，曰禮，至是釐正，凡分房十。

translations.literal: Formerly it was divided into four chambers—Military, Personnel, Household, and Rites; at this point they were reorganized into ten chambers in all.
translations.idiomatic: It had formerly been split into four chambers—Military, Personnel, Household, and Rites—now reorganized into ten chambers in all.

sentences.zh: 其後，又增支馬、小吏二房。

translations.literal: Later, two more chambers were added: Support for Horses and Junior Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Later two more chambers were added: Support for Horses and Junior Clerks.

sentences.zh: 凡房十有二：曰北面房，掌行河北、河東路吏卒，北界邊防、國信事。

translations.literal: There were twelve chambers in all: the Northern Frontier Chamber, which handled clerks and soldiers of Hebei and Hedong circuits, northern frontier defense, and diplomatic credentials.
translations.idiomatic: There were twelve chambers in all. The Northern Frontier Chamber handled clerks and soldiers of the Hebei and Hedong circuits, northern frontier defense, and diplomatic credentials.

sentences.zh: 曰河西房，掌行 陝西路、麟、府、豐、嵐、石、隰州、保德軍吏卒，西界邊防、蕃官。

translations.literal: The Hexi Chamber handled clerks and soldiers of Shaanxi Circuit and of Lin, Fu, Feng, Lan, Shi, Xi, and Sui prefectures and Baode Army, western frontier defense, and frontier tribal officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Hexi Chamber handled clerks and soldiers of Shaanxi Circuit and of Lin, Fu, Feng, Lan, Shi, Xi, and Sui prefectures and Baode Army, western frontier defense, and frontier tribal officials.

sentences.zh: 曰支差房，掌行 調發軍，湖北路邊防及京東、京西、江、淮、廣南東路吏卒，遷補殿侍，選親事官。

translations.literal: The Mobilization Chamber handled mobilized troops, Hubei frontier defense, and clerks and soldiers of Jingdong, Jingxi, Jianghuai, and Guangnan East circuits, promotion of palace attendants, and selection of personal-service officers.
translations.idiomatic: The Mobilization Chamber handled troop mobilizations, Hubei frontier defense, clerks and soldiers of Jingdong, Jingxi, Jianghuai, and eastern Guangnan circuits, promotion of palace attendants, and selection of personal-service officers.

sentences.zh: 曰 在京房，掌行殿前步軍司事，支移兵器，川陝路邊防及畿內、福建路吏卒，軍頭、皇城 司衛兵。

translations.literal: The Capital Chamber handled affairs of the Palace Front Metropolitan Infantry Command, transfer of weapons, Sichuan-Shaanxi frontier defense and clerks and soldiers within the capital region and Fujian Circuit, and soldiers of the Military Commanders and Imperial City offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Capital Chamber handled the Palace Front Metropolitan Infantry Command, weapons transfers, Sichuan-Shaanxi frontier defense, clerks and soldiers in the capital region and Fujian Circuit, and soldiers of the Military Commanders and Imperial City offices.

sentences.zh: 曰教閱房，掌行中外校習，封樁闕額請給，催督驛遞及湖南路邊防。

translations.literal: The Training Chamber handled drill and review at court and in the provinces, requests to fill sealed shortfalls in quotas, and supervision of courier relay stations and Hunan frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: The Training Chamber handled drill and review at court and in the provinces, requests to fill sealed shortfalls in quotas, courier relay supervision, and Hunan frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 曰廣西房 ，掌行招軍捕盜賞罰，廣南西路邊防及兩浙路吏卒。

translations.literal: The Guangxi Chamber handled rewards and punishments for recruiting troops and capturing bandits, Guangnan West frontier defense, and clerks and soldiers of the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangxi Chamber handled rewards and punishments for recruiting troops and capturing bandits, Guangnan West frontier defense, and clerks and soldiers of the Two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 而禁軍轉員，則各隨其房之所領兵 額治之。

translations.literal: Rotation of forbidden troops was administered by whichever chamber held the troop quota in question.
translations.idiomatic: Rotation of forbidden troops fell to whichever chamber held the relevant troop quota.

sentences.zh: 曰兵籍房，掌行諸路將官差發禁兵、選補衛軍文書。

translations.literal: The Military Rolls Chamber handled documents for dispatching forbidden troops and selecting and filling palace guard units in the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Rolls Chamber handled documents dispatching forbidden troops in the circuits and selecting and filling palace guard units.

sentences.zh: 曰民兵房，掌行三路保甲 、弓箭手。

translations.literal: The Militia Chamber handled the Three Circuits' community militia and archer corps.
translations.idiomatic: The Militia Chamber handled community militia and archer corps in the Three Circuits.

sentences.zh: 曰吏房，掌行差將領武臣知州軍、路分都監以上及差內侍官文書。

translations.literal: The Personnel Chamber handled documents appointing military commanders as prefects and circuit supervisors and above, and appointing inner-palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Personnel Chamber handled appointments of military commanders as prefects, regional supervisors and above, and inner-palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 曰知雜房 ，掌行雜務。

translations.literal: The Miscellaneous Affairs Chamber handled miscellaneous business.
translations.idiomatic: The Miscellaneous Affairs Chamber handled miscellaneous business.

sentences.zh: 曰支馬房，掌行內外馬政並坊院監牧吏卒、牧馬、租課。

translations.literal: The Support for Horses Chamber handled horse administration inside and outside the capital, clerks and soldiers of stud farms and pasturage offices, horse husbandry, and pasture rents.
translations.idiomatic: The Support for Horses Chamber handled horse administration inside and outside the capital, clerks and soldiers of stud farms and pasturage offices, horse husbandry, and pasture rents.

sentences.zh: 曰小吏房，掌行 兩省內臣磨勘功過敘用，大使臣已上歷任事狀及校尉以上改轉遷遣。

translations.literal: The Junior Clerks Chamber handled merit review and appointment of inner attendants in the Two Departments, service records of grand emissaries and above, and transfers and assignments of commandants and above.
translations.idiomatic: The Junior Clerks Chamber handled merit review and appointments of inner attendants in the Two Departments, service records of grand emissaries and above, and transfers of commandants and above.

sentences.zh: 吏三十有八：逐房 副承旨三人，主事五人，守闕主事二人，令史十三人，書令史十五人。

translations.literal: Clerks numbered thirty-eight in all: three deputy chief secretaries per chamber, five clerks-in-chief, two reserve clerks-in-chief, thirteen clerks, and fifteen document clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks totaled thirty-eight: three deputy chief secretaries per chamber, five clerks-in-chief, two reserve clerks-in-chief, thirteen clerks, and fifteen document clerks.

sentences.zh: 元祐既創支馬、 小吏二房，增令史為十四人，書令史十九人，創正名貼房十八人。

translations.literal: After the Yuanyou era created the Support for Horses and Junior Clerks chambers, clerks were increased to fourteen and document clerks to nineteen, and eighteen properly titled registry clerks were created.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanyou added the Support for Horses and Junior Clerks chambers, clerks rose to fourteen, document clerks to nineteen, and eighteen properly titled registry clerks were created.

sentences.zh: 大觀增逐房副承旨為 五人，創守闕書令史三人，增正名二十八人。

translations.literal: In the Daguan era deputy chief secretaries per chamber were increased to five, three reserve document clerks were created, and properly titled posts rose to twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daguan, deputy chief secretaries per chamber rose to five, three reserve document clerks were added, and properly titled posts to twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 中書、密院既稱「二府」，每朝奏事，與中書先後上殿。

translations.literal: Once the Secretariat and Military Bureau were styled the "Two Offices," at each court session they reported affairs, mounting the hall before or after the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Once styled the "Two Offices," the Secretariat and Military Bureau reported at court in turn, one mounting the hall before or after the other.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，二邊用兵，知制誥富 弼建言，邊事係國安危，不當專委樞密。

translations.literal: During the Qingli era, when both frontiers saw military action, Drafting Academician Fu Bi submitted that frontier affairs concerned the realm's safety and ought not be entrusted solely to the Military Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingli, with war on both frontiers, Drafting Academician Fu Bi argued that frontier affairs touched the realm's safety and should not rest solely with the Military Bureau.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以為然，即詔中書同議。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong agreed and ordered the Secretariat to deliberate jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong agreed and ordered the Secretariat to join in deliberation.

sentences.zh: 諫官張方平亦言 中書宜知兵事，乃以宰相呂夷簡、章得像並兼樞密使。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Zhang Fangping also said the Secretariat should know military affairs; thus Grand Councillors Lü Yijian and Zhang Dexiang were concurrently appointed commissioners of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Zhang Fangping likewise urged that the Secretariat should know military affairs; Grand Councillors Lü Yijian and Zhang Dexiang were therefore made concurrent commissioners of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，滕甫言：「中書、密院 議邊事，多不合。

translations.literal: Early in Xining, Teng Fu said: "When the Secretariat and Military Bureau deliberate frontier affairs, they often disagree.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xining, Teng Fu said: "When the Secretariat and Military Bureau discuss frontier affairs, they often disagree.

sentences.zh: 趙明與西人戰，中書賞功，而密院降約束；

translations.literal: When Zhao Ming fought the Westerners, the Secretariat rewarded merit while the Military Bureau issued restrictive orders;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Ming fought the Westerners, the Secretariat rewarded his merit while the Military Bureau sent restrictive orders;

sentences.zh: 郭逵修堡柵，密院方詰之 ，而中書以下褒詔。

translations.literal: when Guo Kui repaired fortifications and palisades, the Military Bureau was still investigating him while the Secretariat issued a commendatory edict.
translations.idiomatic: when Guo Kui repaired fortifications, the Military Bureau was still investigating him even as the Secretariat issued a commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 願大臣凡戰守、除帥，議同而後下。

translations.literal: May great ministers agree on all warfare, defense, and commander appointments before orders go down."
translations.idiomatic: Let great ministers agree on warfare, defense, and commander appointments before any order is issued."

sentences.zh: 」神宗善之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong approved.

sentences.zh: 元祐四年，知樞 密院安燾以母憂去職，樞密院官偶獨員。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanyou, An Tao, commissioner of the Military Bureau, left office on mourning for his mother; for a time the bureau had only one senior official.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 4, An Tao, commissioner of the Military Bureau, left on mourning for his mother, leaving the bureau with only one senior official for a time.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫梁燾、司諫劉安世言：「國朝革五代 之弊，文、武二柄，未嘗專付一人，乞依故事命大臣兼領。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Grandee Liang Tao and Investigating Censor Liu Anshi said: "Our dynasty reformed the abuses of the Five Dynasties; the civil and military handles have never been entrusted to a single person—we beg that a great minister be appointed to head it concurrently, per precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Grandee Liang Tao and Investigating Censor Liu Anshi said: "Our dynasty reformed Five Dynasties abuses; civil and military power have never been given to one man alone—we ask that a great minister head the bureau concurrently, as in past practice."

sentences.zh: 」靖康元年，知樞密院事李 綱言：「在祖宗之時，樞密掌兵籍、虎符，三衙管諸軍，率臣主兵柄，各有分守，所以 維持軍政，萬世不易之法。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, Li Gang, commissioner of military affairs, said: "Under the ancestors the Military Bureau held military rolls and tiger tallies, the Three Commands directed the armies, and leading ministers held the military handle—each had its division of responsibility, the unchanging law for maintaining military government through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang 1, Li Gang, commissioner of military affairs, said: "Under the ancestors the Military Bureau held military rolls and tiger tallies, the Three Commands directed the armies, and leading ministers held the military handle—each with its own charge, the unchanging law of military government for all time.

sentences.zh: 自童貫以領樞密院事為宣撫使，既主兵權，又掌兵籍、虎符 ，今日不可不戒。

translations.literal: Since Tong Guan served as commissioner while also being pacification commissioner, holding both military authority and military rolls and tiger tallies, this must not be allowed today.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tong Guan held the bureau while serving as pacification commissioner, wielding both military authority and the rolls and tallies, that must not be allowed now.

sentences.zh: 乞將團結到勤王正兵並付制置使，行營司兵付三衙。

translations.literal: We beg that loyal troops mobilized for the throne be placed under the disposition commissioner, and campaign troops under the Three Commands."
translations.idiomatic: Let loyal troops mobilized for the throne be placed under the disposition commissioner, and campaign troops under the Three Commands."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 樞密使 知院事 同知院事 樞密副使 簽書院事 同簽書院事

translations.literal: Commissioner of Military Affairs; Director of the Bureau; Associate Director; Vice Commissioner; Signing Secretary of the Bureau; Associate Signing Secretary
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of Military Affairs; Director of the Bureau; Associate Director; Vice Commissioner; Signing Secretary of the Bureau; Associate Signing Secretary

sentences.zh: 樞密使、知院事，佐天子執兵政，而同知、副使、簽書為之貳。

translations.literal: The commissioner and director assist the Son of Heaven in wielding military government; associate directors, vice commissioners, and signing secretaries serve as their deputies.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner and director assisted the Son of Heaven in military government; associate directors, vice commissioners, and signing secretaries served as deputies.

sentences.zh: 凡邊防軍旅之常務，與 三省分班稟奏；

translations.literal: Routine frontier and military affairs were reported to the throne in rotation with the Three Departments;
translations.idiomatic: Routine frontier and military business was reported in rotation with the Three Departments;

sentences.zh: 事幹國體，則宰相、執政官合奏；

translations.literal: matters touching the body politic were jointly memorialized by the grand councillor and executive officials;
translations.idiomatic: matters touching the body politic were jointly memorialized by the grand councillor and executive officials;

sentences.zh: 大祭祀則迭為獻官。

translations.literal: at major sacrifices they took turns as offering officials.
translations.idiomatic: at major sacrifices they alternated as offering officials.

sentences.zh: 國初，官無定制，有使則置副，有知院則置同知院，資淺則用直學士簽書院事。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state offices were not fixed; when there was a commissioner a deputy was appointed; when there was a director an associate director was appointed; junior rank used Hanlin Academician to sign bureau business.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding, offices were not fixed: a commissioner had a deputy, a director an associate director, and junior men served as signing secretaries as Hanlin Academicians.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元 年，文彥博、呂公弼為使，韓維、邵亢為副使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining, Wen Yanbo and Lü Gongbi were commissioners; Han Wei and Shao Kang were vice commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 1, Wen Yanbo and Lü Gongbi were commissioners; Han Wei and Shao Kang vice commissioners.

sentences.zh: 時陳升之三至樞府，神宗欲稍異其禮， 乃以為知院事。

translations.literal: Chen Shengzhi had then entered the bureau three times; the emperor wished to vary the ritual slightly and therefore made him director.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shengzhi had entered the bureau three times; the emperor wished to vary the ritual slightly and made him director.

sentences.zh: 於是知院與使、副並置。

translations.literal: Thus director and commissioner, and deputy, were all in place together.
translations.idiomatic: Director, commissioner, and deputy were therefore all in place together.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，將改官制，議者欲廢密院歸兵部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng, as the official system was to be reformed, some proposed abolishing the bureau and returning military affairs to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng 5, as the official system was to be reformed, some proposed abolishing the bureau and returning military affairs to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「祖宗不以兵柄歸有司，故專命官以統之，互相維制，何可廢也？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The ancestors did not place the military handle in the regular offices, but appointed special officials to command it, with mutual checks—how can this be abolished?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Our ancestors did not place the military handle in the regular offices but appointed special officials with mutual checks—how can that be abolished?"

sentences.zh: 」於是得不廢 。

translations.literal: Thus it was not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: So it was not abolished.

sentences.zh: 帝又以樞密聯職輔弼，非出使之官，乃定置知院、同知院二人，使、副悉罷。

translations.literal: The emperor also held that the Military Bureau was linked to assisting governance and was not an envoy post; he therefore fixed two directors and associate directors and abolished commissioners and deputies entirely.
translations.idiomatic: He also held that the bureau assisted governance rather than serving as an envoy post; he fixed two directors and associate directors and abolished commissioners and deputies entirely.

sentences.zh: 元祐初 ，復置簽書院事，仍以樞密直學士充。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanyou, Signing Secretary of the Bureau was restored, again filled by direct Hanlin Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou the post of Signing Secretary was restored, again filled by direct Hanlin Academicians.

sentences.zh: 同簽書樞密院事，治平末，以殿前都虞候郭逵為 之，又以逵判渭州。

translations.literal: Associate Signing Secretary of the Military Bureau: at the end of the Zhiping era, Guo Kui, chief adjutant of the Palace Front Command, was appointed; he was also assigned to govern Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Signing Secretary: late in Zhiping, Palace Front chief adjutant Guo Kui was appointed and also assigned to govern Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 帝初即位，中丞王陶、御史呂景等皆言之。

translations.literal: When the emperor first took the throne, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Tao and Investigating Censor Lü Jing and others all spoke on this.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first took the throne, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Tao and Investigating Censor Lü Jing and others all objected.

sentences.zh: 逵歸，改除宣徽南院使 、知鄆州，自是不復置。

translations.literal: When Kui returned he was reassigned as commissioner of the Southern Palace Attendants Bureau and prefect of Yanzhou; the post was never again established.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui returned he was made commissioner of the Southern Palace Attendants Bureau and prefect of Yanzhou; the post was never restored.

sentences.zh: 政和六年，以內侍童貫權簽書樞密院河西、北面房事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenghe, the inner attendant Tong Guan was made acting Signing Secretary for the Hexi and Northern Frontier chambers.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 6 the inner attendant Tong Guan was made acting Signing Secretary for the Hexi and Northern Frontier chambers.

sentences.zh: 七年， 貫宣撫陝西、河東北三路，帶同簽書樞密院。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Guan pacified Shaanxi and the three northeastern circuits, bearing concurrent Associate Signing Secretary of the Military Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Guan pacified Shaanxi and the three northeastern circuits as concurrent Associate Signing Secretary.

sentences.zh: 既而詔元豐官制即無同簽書樞密院事，改 為權領樞密院。

translations.literal: An edict then stated that the Yuanfeng official system had no Associate Signing Secretary and changed the title to Acting Head of the Military Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then noted that Yuanfeng had no Associate Signing Secretary and changed his title to Acting Head of the Military Bureau.

sentences.zh: 然簽書院事，元豐亦未嘗置。

translations.literal: Yet Signing Secretary had also never been established under Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Signing Secretary itself had never been established under Yuanfeng either.

sentences.zh: 宣和元年，詔童貫領樞密院事，後復以鄭 居中為之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanhe, Tong Guan was ordered to head the Military Bureau; later Zheng Juzhong was also appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 1 Tong Guan was ordered to head the bureau; later Zheng Juzhong was appointed as well.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，置御營司，以宰相為之使。

translations.literal: Early in Jianyan, the Imperial Camp Office was established with the grand councillor as its commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyan the Imperial Camp Office was established with the grand councillor as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，罷，以其事歸樞密院機速房，命宰相范宗尹 兼知樞密院。

translations.literal: In the fourth year it was abolished and its duties returned to the bureau's Rapid Affairs Chamber; Grand Councillor Fan Zongyin was ordered to serve concurrently as director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year it was abolished and its duties returned to the bureau's Rapid Affairs Chamber; Grand Councillor Fan Zongyin was ordered to serve concurrently as director.

sentences.zh: 紹興七年，詔：「樞密本兵之地，事權宜重。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shaoxing an edict said: "The Military Bureau is the seat of military affairs; its authority ought to be weighty.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 7 an edict said: "The Military Bureau is the seat of military affairs; its authority ought to be weighty.

sentences.zh: 可依故事置樞密使，以宰相 張浚兼之。

translations.literal: The post of commissioner may be established per precedent, with Grand Councillor Zhang Jun holding it concurrently."
translations.idiomatic: Let the post of commissioner be restored per precedent, with Grand Councillor Zhang Jun holding it concurrently."

sentences.zh: 」又詔立班序立依宰相例。

translations.literal: Another edict fixed court precedence according to the grand councillor's example.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict fixed court precedence on the grand councillor's model.

sentences.zh: 其後或兼或否。

translations.literal: Thereafter the post was sometimes held concurrently and sometimes not.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter it was sometimes held concurrently and sometimes not.

sentences.zh: 至開禧，以宰臣兼使，遂為永制 。

translations.literal: By Kaixi, with the chief minister holding the commissionership concurrently, this became permanent practice.
translations.idiomatic: By Kaixi, with the chief minister holding the commission concurrently, this became permanent practice.

sentences.zh: 使與知院，同知、副使，亦或併除，其簽書、同簽書並為端明殿學士，恩數特依執政 ，或以武臣為之，亦異典也。

translations.literal: Commissioner and director, associate and vice, were sometimes appointed together; signing and associate signing secretaries were usually Terminal Bright Hall Academicians with executive perquisites, or sometimes military officials—an exceptional arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner, director, associate, and vice were sometimes appointed together; signing secretaries were usually Terminal Bright Hall Academicians with executive perquisites, or occasionally military men—an exceptional arrangement.

sentences.zh: 都承旨 副都承旨

translations.literal: Chief Secretary; Deputy Chief Secretary
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretary; Deputy Chief Secretary

sentences.zh: 掌承宣旨命，通領院務。

translations.literal: They received and proclaimed imperial orders and directed overall bureau business.
translations.idiomatic: They received and proclaimed imperial orders and directed overall bureau business.

sentences.zh: 若便殿侍立，閱試禁衛兵校，則隨事敷奏，承所得旨以授有司 ，蕃國入見亦如之。

translations.literal: When attending in the side hall, or when reviewing forbidden guard troops, they reported as the occasion required and transmitted received intent to the relevant offices; the same applied when foreign states came to audience.
translations.idiomatic: When attending in the side hall or reviewing forbidden guard troops, they reported as required and transmitted received intent to the proper offices; the same applied when foreign states came to audience.

sentences.zh: 檢察主事以下功過及遷補之事。

translations.literal: They inspected merit and faults of clerks-in-chief and below and matters of promotion and reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: They inspected merit and faults of clerks-in-chief and below and handled promotions and reassignments.

sentences.zh: 都承旨，舊用院吏遞遷。

translations.literal: The chief secretary had formerly been promoted from bureau clerks in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The chief secretary had formerly been promoted in turn from bureau clerks.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年 ，始以東上合門使李評為之，又以皇城使李綬為之副，更用士人自評、綬始。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, Eastern Upper Gatehouse usher Li Ping was first appointed; Imperial City commissioner Li Shou was made deputy—scholar-officials were first used from Ping and Shou onward.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 3, Eastern Upper Gatehouse usher Li Ping was first appointed, with Imperial City commissioner Li Shou as deputy—scholar-officials were first used from Ping and Shou onward.

sentences.zh: 是月，詔 都承旨、副都承旨見樞密使、副如合門使禮。

translations.literal: That month an edict ordered chief and deputy chief secretaries to observe toward commissioners and deputies the same ritual as Gatehouse ushers.
translations.idiomatic: That month an edict ordered chief and deputy chief secretaries to observe toward commissioners and deputies the same ritual as Gatehouse ushers.

sentences.zh: 五年，以同修起居注曾孝寬兼都承旨，參 用儒臣自孝寬始。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Co-revising Academician for the Diary Zeng Xiaokuan was made concurrent chief secretary—scholar-officials were first used in this mixed role from Xiaokuan onward.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Co-revising Academician for the Diary Zeng Xiaokuan was made concurrent chief secretary—mixed appointment of scholar-officials began with Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 元豐四年，客省使張誠一為都承旨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanfeng, Guest Reception Commissioner Zhang Chengyi was chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng 4, Guest Reception Commissioner Zhang Chengyi was chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 都承旨復用武臣，自誠一始。

translations.literal: Military officials were again used as chief secretaries, beginning with Chengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials were again used as chief secretaries, beginning with Chengyi.

sentences.zh: 元 祐初，復以文臣為都承旨。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanyou, scholar-officials were again made chief secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou scholar-officials were again made chief secretaries.

sentences.zh: 其後以待制充。

translations.literal: Thereafter awaiting commissioners filled the post.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter awaiting commissioners filled the post.

sentences.zh: 元符三年，王師約為都承旨，左司諫陳瓘言 ：「神考以文臣為都承旨，其副則參求外戚武臣之可用者。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfu, Wang Shiyue was chief secretary; Left Remonstrance Censor Chen Guan said: "Emperor Shenzong used scholar-officials as chief secretaries; for the deputy he sought usable military affines from outside the kin.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 3, Wang Shiyue was chief secretary; Left Remonstrance Censor Chen Guan said: "Shenzong used scholar-officials as chief secretaries and sought capable military affines for the deputy.

sentences.zh: 今師約未曆邊任，擢置樞屬 掾文臣之位，甚非神考設官之意。

translations.literal: Now Shiyue has never served on the frontier yet is raised to a bureau clerk post reserved for scholar-officials—this greatly departs from Shenzong's intent in establishing the office."
translations.idiomatic: Shiyue has never served on the frontier yet is raised to a scholar-official clerk post in the bureau—far from Shenzong's intent in establishing the office."

sentences.zh: 」至崇寧以後，專用武臣。

translations.literal: From Chongning onward military officials alone were used.
translations.idiomatic: From Chongning onward only military officials were used.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，高宗在會稽，以武臣辛道宗為都承旨，頗用事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan, when Gaozong was at Kuaiji, the military official Xin Daozong was chief secretary and wielded considerable influence.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 4, when Gaozong was at Kuaiji, military official Xin Daozong was chief secretary and wielded considerable influence.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，道宗既免，乃詔 依元祐職制，都承旨以兩制為之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, after Daozong was removed, an edict restored the Yuanyou system: the chief secretary was to be drawn from the Two Drafts.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 1, after Daozong was removed, an edict restored the Yuanyou system: the chief secretary was to be drawn from the Two Drafts.

sentences.zh: 如未曾任侍從之人，即依權侍郎法，又或加學士、待 制、修撰貼職。

translations.literal: If the appointee had never served as palace attendant, he followed the rule for acting vice ministers; sometimes the additional titles of academician, awaiting commissioner, compiler, or registry clerk were added.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had never served as palace attendants followed the rule for acting vice ministers; sometimes titles such as academician, awaiting commissioner, compiler, or registry clerk were added.

sentences.zh: 乾道初，再用武臣，自張說始。

translations.literal: Early in Qiandao, military officials were again used, beginning with Zhang Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiandao military officials were again appointed, beginning with Zhang Yue.

sentences.zh: 淳熙九年，都承旨復用士人，自蕭燧始 。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chunxi, scholar-officials were again made chief secretaries, beginning with Xiao Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 9 scholar-officials again held the chief secretary post, beginning with Xiao Sui.

sentences.zh: 副都承旨文、武通除。

translations.literal: Deputy chief secretaries were appointed from both civil and military ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy chief secretaries could be drawn from either civil or military ranks.

sentences.zh: 檢詳官

translations.literal: Examining Officer
translations.idiomatic: Examining Officer

sentences.zh: 熙寧四年置，視中書檢正官。

translations.literal: Established in the fourth year of Xining, on the model of examining officers of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Xining 4, modeled on the Secretariat's examining officers.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，定以三員，及改官制，罷之。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanfeng the number was fixed at three; when the official system was reformed, the post was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanfeng the post was fixed at three; under the reformed official system it was abolished.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，復置檢 詳兩員，敘位在左、右司之下。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan two examining officers were restored, ranking below the Left and Right Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 3 two examining officers were restored, ranking below the Left and Right Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年減一員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing one post was cut.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 2 one post was eliminated.

translations.literal: Planning Officer
translations.idiomatic: Planning Officer

translations.idiomatic: Four posts.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan the Imperial Camp Office was abolished and merged into the Military Bureau as the Rapid Affairs Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 4 the Imperial Camp Office was abolished and merged into the Military Bureau as the Rapid Affairs Chamber.

sentences.zh: 隨司減罷屬官，置幹辦官四員， 詔並改為計議官。

translations.literal: Subordinate offices of the dissolved agency were reduced; four handling officers were established and by edict all were renamed Planning Officers.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate posts of the dissolved office were cut; four handling officers were set up and by edict renamed Planning Officers.

sentences.zh: 至紹興十一年減罷。

translations.literal: By the eleventh year of Shaoxing they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: By Shaoxing 11 they were abolished.

translations.literal: Compiling Officer
translations.idiomatic: Compiling Officer

translations.idiomatic: Appointed as tasks required without fixed quota; concurrent bureau officials did not carry the title on the roster.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，以王存、顧臨等同編修經武要略 ，兼刪定諸房例冊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, Wang Cun, Gu Lin, and others jointly compiled Essentials of Military Institutions and concurrently revised the precedent registers of the various chambers.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 3, Wang Cun, Gu Lin, and others jointly compiled Essentials of Military Institutions and revised the precedent registers of the various chambers.

sentences.zh: 初擬都、副承旨提舉，神宗謂存等皆館職，不欲令承旨提舉，詔改 為管幹。

translations.literal: At first the chief and deputy secretaries were to direct it; the emperor said Cun and the others all held academy posts and should not be directed by the secretaries, and ordered the title changed to "supervising."
translations.idiomatic: At first chief and deputy secretaries were to direct it; Shenzong said Cun and the others held academy posts and should not answer to the secretaries, and ordered the role retitled "supervising."

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年，編修刑部、軍馬司事，令都、副承旨兼領。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaosheng, compiling affairs of the Ministry of Justice and Horse and Military Bureau were placed under joint charge of the chief and deputy secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng 4, compilation of Ministry of Justice and Horse and Military Bureau affairs was placed under joint charge of the chief and deputy secretaries.

sentences.zh: 政和七年，編修北邊條 例，又別置詳覆官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenghe, northern frontier regulations were compiled and a separate detailed review officer was also appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 7 northern frontier regulations were compiled and a separate detailed review officer was appointed.

translations.literal: Deliberation Office
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation Office

translations.idiomatic: Supervisors of the gates of the Three Departments and Military Bureau

sentences.zh: 舊係差小使臣及內侍官充。

translations.literal: Formerly filled by dispatched junior envoys and inner-palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly filled by dispatched junior envoys and inner-palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 嘉定六年，詔以曾經作縣、通判資序人充。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiading an edict ordered that persons who had served as county magistrate or transit intendant might be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading 6 an edict required appointees to have served as county magistrate or transit intendant.

sentences.zh: 小使臣省罷，內 侍官改以三省、樞密院門機察官繫銜。

translations.literal: Junior envoys were eliminated; inner attendants were retitled with the concurrent post of gate inspector of the Three Departments and Military Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Junior envoys were eliminated; inner attendants were retitled with the concurrent post of gate inspector of the Three Departments and Military Bureau.

sentences.zh: 主管三省、樞密院架閤文字 一員，嘉定八年置，以選人、京朝官通差。

translations.literal: One officer in charge of archive documents of the Three Departments and Military Bureau, established in the eighth year of Jiading, filled by rotation from selection officials and capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: One officer in charge of archive documents of the Three Departments and Military Bureau, established in Jiading 8, filled by rotation from selection and capital officials.

sentences.zh: 三省、樞密院激賞庫 三省、樞密院激賞酒庫

translations.literal: Reward Treasury of the Three Departments and Military Bureau; Reward Wine Treasury of the Three Departments and Military Bureau
translations.idiomatic: Reward Treasury of the Three Departments and Military Bureau; Reward Wine Treasury of the Three Departments and Military Bureau

translations.literal: Two supervising officers each.
translations.idiomatic: Two supervising officers each.

translations.literal: (At first military officials; at the end of Jiatai, selection officials were first used.)
translations.idiomatic: (At first military officials; at the end of Jiatai selection officials were first used.)

sentences.zh: 二庫並因紹興用兵，創以備邊；

translations.literal: Both treasuries were created during Shaoxing military campaigns to prepare the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Both treasuries were created during Shaoxing's wars to prepare the frontier;

sentences.zh: 後 兵罷，專以備堂、東兩廚應幹宰執支遣。

translations.literal: after hostilities ceased they served solely to meet disbursements of the Hall and Eastern kitchens for grand councillors and executive officials.
translations.idiomatic: after fighting ended they supplied only the Hall and Eastern kitchens for grand councillors and executive officials.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷軍期急速錢物金帶，以備激犒；

translations.literal: If the court needed urgent funds, goods, or gold belts for military deadlines, they were kept for prompt rewards;
translations.idiomatic: When the court needed urgent cash, goods, or gold belts for military deadlines, they were kept for prompt rewards;

sentences.zh: 諸軍將 帥告命綾紙，以備科撥調遣等用。

translations.literal: silk paper for army commanders' commissions was kept for allocation and dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: silk paper for commanders' commissions was kept for allocation and dispatch.

sentences.zh: 省、院、府吏胥之給，亦取具焉。

translations.literal: Stipends for clerks of the Departments, bureau, and offices were also drawn from them.
translations.idiomatic: Stipends for Department, bureau, and office clerks were also drawn from them.

sentences.zh: 御營使 提舉修政局 制國用使 都督諸路軍馬

translations.literal: Imperial Camp Commissioner; Commissioner for Government Renewal; Commissioner for State Revenue; Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in All Circuits
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Camp Commissioner; Commissioner for Government Renewal; Commissioner for State Revenue; Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in All Circuits

sentences.zh: 中興，多以宰相兼領兵政、財用之事，而執政同預焉。

translations.literal: After the restoration, grand councillors often concurrently headed military and fiscal affairs, with executive officials joining in.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, grand councillors often concurrently directed military and fiscal affairs, with executive officials participating.

sentences.zh: 因事創名，未久遄罷，可以不書 。

translations.literal: Titles were created for particular occasions and soon abolished—they need not be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Titles were created for particular occasions and soon abolished and need not be recorded.

sentences.zh: 以其關宰相設施，因記其名稱本末附見焉。

translations.literal: Because they concern arrangements made by grand councillors, their names and origins are recorded here for reference.
translations.idiomatic: Because they concern grand councillors' arrangements, their names and origins are recorded here for reference.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，置御營司，以宰相為之使，仍以執政官兼副使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan the Imperial Camp Office was established with the grand councillor as commissioner and executive officials as concurrent deputy commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 1 the Imperial Camp Office was established with the grand councillor as commissioner and executive officials as deputy commissioners.

sentences.zh: 其屬有參贊軍事，以侍從官 兼；

translations.literal: Its subordinates included a military affairs adviser, filled concurrently by palace attendants;
translations.idiomatic: Its staff included a military affairs adviser, filled by palace attendants;

sentences.zh: 提舉一行事務，以大將兼。

translations.literal: and an officer directing all traveling business, filled by a major general.
translations.idiomatic: and an officer directing all traveling business, filled by a major general.

sentences.zh: 其將佐有都統制及五軍統制以下官。

translations.literal: Its staff officers included a commander-in-chief and commanders of the five armies and below.
translations.idiomatic: Its officers included a commander-in-chief and commanders of the five armies and below.

sentences.zh: 初以總齊行在軍中 之政。

translations.literal: At first it coordinated military government in the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: At first it coordinated military affairs at the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔御營使司止管行在五軍營砦事務，其餘應幹邊防措置等事，釐正歸三省 、樞密院。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict limited the Imperial Camp Office to managing the five armies' camps and fortifications at the traveling capital; other frontier measures were reorganized under the Three Departments and Military Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict limited the office to the five armies' camps at the traveling capital; other frontier business returned to the Three Departments and Military Bureau.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔自今宰相兼知樞密院事，罷御營使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict ordered that henceforth the grand councillor would concurrently direct the Military Bureau and the Imperial Camp commissioner was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year an edict ordered the grand councillor to concurrently direct the Military Bureau and abolished the Imperial Camp commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時臣僚言：「宰相之職，無所 不統。

translations.literal: At the time officials said: "The grand councillor's duty embraces everything.
translations.idiomatic: Officials then said: "The grand councillor's duty embraces everything.

sentences.zh: 本朝沿五代之制，政事分為兩府，兵權付於樞密，比年又置御營使，是政出於三 也。

translations.literal: Our dynasty follows Five Dynasties practice: civil affairs are split between two offices and military power is given to the Military Bureau; in recent years an Imperial Camp commissioner was added—government issues from three sources.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty follows Five Dynasties practice: civil affairs split between two offices and military power to the Military Bureau; recently an Imperial Camp commissioner was added—policy issued from three sources.

translations.literal: (established in the fourth year of Xianping.)
translations.idiomatic: (established in Xianping 4.)

sentences.zh: 以判磨勘司兼掌。

translations.literal: held concurrently by the Chief Audit judge.
translations.idiomatic: held concurrently by the Chief Audit judge.

sentences.zh: 凡支收財利未結絕者，籍其名件而督之。

translations.literal: All revenue and goods not yet settled were registered by name and supervised.
translations.idiomatic: All unsettled revenue and goods were registered by name and supervised.

sentences.zh: 都理欠司，

translations.literal: Chief Arrears Office,
translations.idiomatic: Chief Arrears Office,

sentences.zh: （雍熙二年，三部各置理欠，有勾簿司，景德四年廢。）〉

translations.literal: (In the second year of Yongxi each department established an arrears office; there was an account-book office; abolished in the fourth year of Jingde.)
translations.idiomatic: (In Yongxi 2 each department had an arrears office and account-book office; abolished in Jingde 4.)

sentences.zh: 判司官一人，以朝 官充。

translations.literal: One judge, filled by a capital official.
translations.idiomatic: One judge, filled by a capital official.

sentences.zh: 掌理在京及天下欠負官物之籍，皆立限以促之。

translations.literal: It handled registers of arrears in official goods at the capital and throughout the realm, all with deadlines for collection.
translations.idiomatic: It handled registers of official-goods arrears at the capital and throughout the realm, all with collection deadlines.

sentences.zh: 都憑由司，以判都理欠司官兼，掌在京官物支破之事。

translations.literal: Chief Voucher Office, held concurrently by the Chief Arrears judge, directed disbursement of official goods at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Voucher Office, held by the Chief Arrears judge, directed capital disbursements of official goods.

sentences.zh: 凡部支官物，皆覆視無虛謬，則 印署而還之，支訖，復據數送勾而銷破之。

translations.literal: All departmental disbursements were reviewed for false entries; if none, they were sealed and returned; after disbursement, numbers were sent to audit for cancellation.
translations.idiomatic: All departmental disbursements were reviewed; if sound, sealed and returned; after disbursement, numbers went to audit for cancellation.

sentences.zh: 開拆司，判司官一人，以朝官充。

translations.literal: Opening and Sorting Office: one judge, filled by a capital official.
translations.idiomatic: Opening and Sorting Office: one judge, filled by a capital official.

sentences.zh: 掌受宣敕及諸州申牒之籍，發放以付三部，兼掌發放 、勾鑿、催驅、受事。

translations.literal: It received edicts and provincial memorials, distributed them to the three departments, and also directed distribution, checking, urging, and receipt of business.
translations.idiomatic: It received edicts and provincial memorials, distributed them to the three departments, and directed distribution, checking, urging, and receipt.

sentences.zh: 發放司，掌受三司帖牒而下之。

translations.literal: Distribution Office directed receipt of the three departments' posted documents for dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Distribution Office directed receipt of the three departments' posted documents.

sentences.zh: （太平興國年中置。）〉

translations.literal: (established in the Taiping Xingguo era.)
translations.idiomatic: (established in the Taiping Xingguo era.)

sentences.zh: 勾鑿司，掌勾校三部公事簿帳。

translations.literal: Checking Office audited the account books of the three departments' public business.
translations.idiomatic: Checking Office audited the three departments' public account books.

sentences.zh: 催驅司，掌督京城諸司庫務末帳，京畿倉場庫務月帳憑由送勾，及三部支訖內外奉祿之 事。

translations.literal: Urging Office supervised end-of-term accounts of capital offices and storehouses, monthly vouchers of capital-region granaries and storehouses sent for audit, and inner and outer salary disbursements of the three departments.
translations.idiomatic: Urging Office supervised capital offices' end accounts, capital-region granary monthly vouchers, and three departments' salary disbursements.

sentences.zh: 受事司，掌諸處解送諸色名籍，以發付三部。

translations.literal: Receipt Office received registers of various categories submitted from all places for dispatch to the three departments.
translations.idiomatic: Receipt Office received registers from all places for dispatch to the three departments.

sentences.zh: 衙司管轄官二人，以判開拆司官及內侍都知、押班充。

translations.literal: Two yamen supervisory officers, filled by the Opening and Sorting judge and the inner attendant director and duty officer.
translations.idiomatic: Two yamen supervisory officers, filled by the Opening judge and inner attendant director and duty officer.

sentences.zh: 掌大將、軍將名籍，第其勞而均 其役使。

translations.literal: They directed registers of great generals and military officers, ranked their labor, and equalized their assignments.
translations.idiomatic: They directed great generals' and military officers' registers, ranked labor, and equalized assignments.

sentences.zh: 勾當公事官二員，以朝官充。

translations.literal: Two public-business handling officers, filled by capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: Two public-business handling officers, filled by capital officials.

sentences.zh: 掌分左右廂檢計、定奪、點檢、覆驗、估剝之事。

translations.literal: They directed inspection, determination, checking, re-verification, and appraisal and stripping of the left and right wings.
translations.idiomatic: They directed inspection, determination, checking, re-verification, and appraisal of the left and right wings.

sentences.zh: 三司推 勘公事一人，以京朝官充。

translations.literal: One Three Commissions investigating public-business officer, filled by a capital official.
translations.idiomatic: One investigating public-business officer, filled by a capital official.

sentences.zh: 掌推劾諸部公事。

translations.literal: Directed investigation of public business in all departments.
translations.idiomatic: Directed investigation of all departments' public business.

sentences.zh: 勾當諸司、馬步軍糧料院官各一人，以京朝官充。

translations.literal: One handling officer each for all offices and the Infantry and Cavalry Army Rations Office, filled by capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: One handling officer each for all offices and the Infantry and Cavalry Army Rations Office, filled by capital officials.

sentences.zh: 掌文武官諸司、諸軍給受奉料，批書 券曆，諸倉庫案驗而稟賦之。

translations.literal: They directed salaries for civil and military officials, all offices, and all armies, wrote vouchers on registers, and after storehouse sections verified, reported for disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: They directed civil and military salaries, wrote vouchers, and after storehouse verification reported for disbursement.

sentences.zh: 勾當馬步軍專勾司官一人，以京朝官充。

translations.literal: One dedicated checking officer for infantry and cavalry armies, filled by a capital official.
translations.idiomatic: One dedicated infantry and cavalry checking officer, filled by a capital official.

sentences.zh: （舊以三班。）〉

translations.literal: (formerly filled from the Three Ranks.)
translations.idiomatic: (formerly filled from the Three Ranks.)

sentences.zh: 掌諸軍兵馬逃亡收並之籍，諸 司庫務給受之數，審校其欺詐，批曆以送糧料院。

translations.literal: Directed registers of army deserters recovered, numbers of storehouse disbursements, examined fraud, and endorsed registers sent to the Rations Office.
translations.idiomatic: Directed deserter recovery registers, storehouse disbursement numbers, examined fraud, and endorsed registers to the Rations Office.

sentences.zh: 以上並屬三司使。

translations.literal: All the above were subordinate to the Commissioner of the Three Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: All the above were subordinate to the Commissioner of the Three Commissions.

sentences.zh: 元豐官制行，罷三司使並歸戶部。

translations.literal: When the Yuanfeng official system took effect, the Three Commissions commissioner was abolished and duties returned to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanfeng official system took effect, the commissioner was abolished and duties returned to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士院 翰林學士承旨 翰林學士 知制誥 直學士院 翰林權直 學士院權直

translations.literal: Hanlin Academy; Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts; Hanlin Academician; Drafting Academician; Direct Academy; Hanlin Acting Direct; Academy Acting Direct
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academy; Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts; Hanlin Academician; Drafting Academician; Direct Academy; Hanlin Acting Direct; Academy Acting Direct

sentences.zh: 掌制、誥、詔、令撰述之事。

translations.literal: They directed composition of ordinances, patents, edicts, and orders.
translations.idiomatic: They directed composition of ordinances, patents, edicts, and orders.

sentences.zh: 凡立后妃，封親王，拜宰相、樞密使、三公、三少，除開 府儀同三司、節度使，加封，加檢校官，並用制；

translations.literal: For establishing empresses and consorts, enfeoffing imperial princes, appointing grand councillors, military commissioners, the Three Dukes and Three Minors, conferring Grand Preceptor of the State, military commissioners, and additional enfeoffments and probationary posts, ordinances were used;
translations.idiomatic: Establishing empresses, enfeoffing princes, appointing grand councillors and military commissioners, the Three Dukes and Three Minors, Grand Preceptor, military commissioners, and additional honors used ordinances;

sentences.zh: 賜大臣太中大夫、觀察使以上，用批 答及詔書；

translations.literal: for granting great ministers Grand Master of Palace and military commissioners and above, written replies and edict documents were used;
translations.idiomatic: granting great ministers Grand Master of Palace and observation commissioners and above used written replies and edict documents;

sentences.zh: 餘官用敕書；

translations.literal: other officials used commission documents;
translations.idiomatic: other officials used commission documents;

sentences.zh: 布大號令用御札；

translations.literal: great proclamations used imperial letters;
translations.idiomatic: great proclamations used imperial letters;

sentences.zh: 戒勵百官、曉諭軍民用敕榜；

translations.literal: admonitions to all officials and proclamations to armies and people used edict placards;
translations.idiomatic: admonitions to officials and proclamations to armies and people used edict placards;

sentences.zh: 遣使勞問臣下 ，口宣。

translations.literal: dispatching envoys to console ministers used oral edicts.
translations.idiomatic: dispatching envoys to console ministers used oral edicts.

sentences.zh: 凡降大赦、曲赦、德音，則先進草；

translations.literal: For great amnesties, partial amnesties, and grace edicts, a draft was first submitted;
translations.idiomatic: For great amnesties, partial amnesties, and grace edicts, a draft was submitted first;

sentences.zh: 大詔命及外國書，則具本取旨，得畫亦如 之。

translations.literal: for great edict commissions and letters to foreign states, the original was prepared to obtain intent; when approved for drawing, the same applied.
translations.idiomatic: for great edict commissions and foreign letters, the original was prepared for intent; approved drafts were drawn likewise.

sentences.zh: 凡拜宰相及事重者，晚漏上，天子御內東門小殿，宣召面諭，給筆札書所得旨。

translations.literal: For appointing a grand councillor and other weighty matters, after the evening watch the Son of Heaven held court in the inner east gate small hall, summoned for audience to instruct face to face, and brush and paper were given to write received intent.
translations.idiomatic: For appointing a grand councillor and weighty matters, after the evening watch the emperor held court at the inner east gate small hall, instructed face to face, and gave brush and paper to record intent.

sentences.zh: 稟奏歸 院，內侍鎖院門，禁止出入。

translations.literal: Returning to the academy to report, inner attendants locked the gate and exit was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the academy, inner attendants locked the gate and forbade exit.

sentences.zh: 夜漏盡，具詞進入；

translations.literal: When the night watch ended, the text was submitted;
translations.idiomatic: When the night watch ended, the text was submitted;

sentences.zh: 遲明，白麻出，閤門使引授中書，中 書授舍人宣讀。

translations.literal: at dawn white hemp emerged; the Gatehouse usher led delivery to the Secretariat, and the Secretariat gave it to the drafter to proclaim.
translations.idiomatic: at dawn white hemp emerged; the Gatehouse usher delivered it to the Secretariat for the drafter to proclaim.

sentences.zh: 其餘除授並御札，但用御寶封，遣內侍送學士院鎖門而已。

translations.literal: Other appointments used only imperial letters sealed with the imperial treasure and sent by inner attendants to lock the academy gate.
translations.idiomatic: Other appointments used imperial letters sealed with the treasure and sent by inner attendants to lock the academy.

sentences.zh: 至於赦書、 德音，則中書遣吏持送本院，內侍鎖院如除授焉。

translations.literal: As for amnesty documents and grace edicts, the Secretariat sent clerks to deliver them to the academy and inner attendants locked the gate as for appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty and grace edicts were delivered by Secretariat clerks and the gate was locked as for appointments.

sentences.zh: 凡撰述皆寫畫進入，請印署而出，中 書省熟狀亦如之。

translations.literal: All compositions were written, drawn, and submitted for seal before issue; Secretariat approval documents were the same.
translations.idiomatic: All compositions were written, drawn, and submitted for seal; Secretariat approvals were the same.

sentences.zh: 若已畫旨而未盡及舛誤，則論奏貼正。

translations.literal: If drawn but incomplete or erroneous, a memorial was submitted to correct it.
translations.idiomatic: If drawn but incomplete or erroneous, a memorial corrected it.

sentences.zh: 凡宮禁所用文詞皆掌之。

translations.literal: All literary texts used in the palace were under their charge.
translations.idiomatic: All palace literary texts were under their charge.

sentences.zh: 乘輿 行幸，則侍從以備顧問，有獻納則請對，仍不隔班。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage traveled, they attended as companions for consultation; if there were submissions, they requested audience, still without skipping formation.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial travel they attended for consultation; submissions requested audience without skipping formation.

sentences.zh: 凡奏事用榜子，關白三省、樞密院 用諮報，不名。

translations.literal: Memorials used placards; notification to the Three Departments and Military Bureau used consultation reports, without personal names.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials used placards; notification to the Three Departments and Military Bureau used reports without personal names.

sentences.zh: 凡初命為學士，皆遣使就第宣詔旨召入院。

translations.literal: On first appointment as academician, an envoy was sent to the residence to proclaim the edict and summon entry to the academy.
translations.idiomatic: On first appointment, an envoy proclaimed the edict at the residence and summoned entry.

sentences.zh: 上日，敕設會從官，宥以樂。

translations.literal: On the first day an edict ordered a gathering of attendant officials with music provided.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day an edict ordered a gathering of attendant officials with music.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，始命 佩魚，自蒲宗孟始。

translations.literal: In Yuanfeng they were first ordered to wear fish pendants, beginning with Pu Zongmeng.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng they were first ordered to wear fish pendants, beginning with Pu Zongmeng.

sentences.zh: 見執政議事則繫、靴，蓋與侍從異禮也。

translations.literal: When meeting executives to discuss affairs they wore belt and boots—ritual differing from other attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When meeting executives for discussion they wore belt and boots—ritual differing from other attendants.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，強淵明請以前 後所被旨及案例，修為本院敕令格式。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, Qiang Yuanming requested that prior received intents and cases be compiled into statutory commands and formats for the academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 3, Qiang Yuanming requested prior intents and cases be compiled into academy statutory commands and formats.

sentences.zh: 五年，御書摛文堂榜賜學士院。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor personally wrote the hall name "Hall for Drawing Forth Literature" and bestowed it on the academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor wrote the hall name "Drawing Forth Literature" and bestowed it on the academy.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，吳幵 等奏：「大禮鎖院，麻三道以上，係雙學士宿直分撰，乞依故事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, Wu Bian and others memorialized: "For great ritual lock-in of the academy, when three or more white-hemp documents are involved, two academicians on night duty divide the drafting—we beg to follow precedent."
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang 1, Wu Bian and others said: "For great ritual academy lock-in with three or more white-hemp documents, two night-duty academicians should divide drafting per precedent."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 承旨，不常置，以學士久次者為之。

translations.literal: Recipient of Edicts was not regularly established; the academician of longest tenure held it.
translations.idiomatic: Recipient of Edicts was not regularly established; the longest-serving academician held it.

sentences.zh: 凡他官入院未除學士，謂之直院；

translations.literal: When another official entered the academy before appointment as academician, he was called Direct of the Academy;
translations.idiomatic: When another official entered before academician appointment, he was called Direct of the Academy;

sentences.zh: 學士俱闕，他官 暫行院中文書，謂之權直。

translations.literal: when all academicians were vacant, another official temporarily handled academy documents, called Acting Direct.
translations.idiomatic: when all academicians were vacant, another official temporarily handled documents as Acting Direct.

sentences.zh: 自國初至元豐官制行，百司事失其實，多所釐正，獨學士院 承唐舊典不改。

translations.literal: From the founding until the Yuanfeng official system, the hundred offices lost their true functions and much was corrected; only the academy followed Tang precedent unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding until Yuanfeng, the hundred offices lost true functions and much was corrected; only the academy followed Tang precedent unchanged.

sentences.zh: 乾道九年，崔敦詩初以秘書省正字兼翰林權直。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qiandao, Cui Dunshi was first made Hanlin Acting Direct as Rectifier of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 9, Cui Dunshi was first Hanlin Acting Direct as Secretariat Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 淳熙五年，敦詩再入院 ，議者以翰林乃應奉之所，非專掌制誥之地，更為學士院權直。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunxi, Dunshi re-entered the academy; critics said Hanlin was a service post, not solely for drafting patents, and the title was changed to Academy Acting Direct.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 5, Dunshi re-entered; critics said Hanlin was for attendance, not solely patents, and the title became Academy Acting Direct.

sentences.zh: 後復稱翰林權直，然亦 互除不廢，權、正或至三人。

translations.literal: Later it was again called Hanlin Acting Direct, yet mutual appointment continued; acting and regular sometimes reached three.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was again Hanlin Acting Direct, with mutual appointment continuing; acting and regular sometimes reached three.

sentences.zh: 翰林侍讀學士

translations.literal: Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting Academician
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting Academician

sentences.zh: 充宮觀兼侍讀：元豐八年五月，資政殿大學士呂公著兼侍讀，提舉中太乙宮兼集禧觀公 事。

translations.literal: Palace-Abbey Attendant concurrently Reader-in-Waiting: in the fifth month of the eighth year of Yuanfeng, Grand Master of the Hall for Veneration of Governance Lü Gongzhu was concurrent Reader-in-Waiting, directing the Central Supreme Unity Palace and Chiji Blessed Celebration Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant concurrently Reader: Yuanfeng 8.5, Grand Master Lü Gongzhu was Reader-in-Waiting, directing Central Supreme Unity and Chiji Blessed Celebration abbeys.

sentences.zh: 七月，韓維兼侍讀，提舉中太乙宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Han Wei was concurrent Reader-in-Waiting, directing the Central Supreme Unity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Han Wei was concurrent Reader-in-Waiting, directing Central Supreme Unity Palace.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，端明殿學士范鎮致仕，提舉中太乙 宮兼集禧觀公事，兼侍讀，不赴。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, Terminal Bright Hall Academician Fan Zhen retired, directing Central Supreme Unity and Chiji Blessed Celebration, concurrent Reader-in-Waiting, without attending.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 1, Fan Zhen retired, directing the abbeys, concurrent Reader-in-Waiting, without attending.

sentences.zh: 六年，馮京兼侍讀，充太乙宮使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Feng Jing was concurrent Reader-in-Waiting, filling Supreme Unity Palace commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Feng Jing was concurrent Reader-in-Waiting as Supreme Unity commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，乞致仕，不 允，仍免經筵進讀。

translations.literal: Before long he requested retirement; it was denied, but he was excused from lecturing at the classics hall.
translations.idiomatic: He soon requested retirement; denied, but excused from classics-hall lecturing.

sentences.zh: 中興以來，如朱勝非、張浚、謝克家、趙鼎、万俟离並以萬壽觀使 兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Since the restoration, Zhu Shengfei, Zhang Jun, Xie Kejia, Zhao Ding, and Wan Qixie were all Longevity Abbey commissioners concurrently Readers-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Since the restoration, Zhu Shengfei, Zhang Jun, Xie Kejia, Zhao Ding, and Wan Qixie were Longevity Abbey commissioners concurrently Readers.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，張燾以萬壽觀、湯思退以醴泉觀並侍讀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing, Zhang Zhao was Longevity Abbey commissioner and Tang Situo Sweet Spring Abbey commissioner, both Readers-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In Longxing 1, Zhang Zhao was Longevity and Tang Situo Sweet Spring commissioner, both Readers.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年，劉章以佑神觀 兼焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiandao, Liu Zhang was You Spirit Abbey commissioner concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 5, Liu Zhang was You Spirit Abbey commissioner concurrently.

sentences.zh: 臺諫兼侍讀：自慶曆以來，臺丞多兼侍讀，諫長未有兼者。

translations.literal: Censorate and Remonstrance concurrently Reader-in-Waiting: since Qingli, censor deputies often held Reader-in-Waiting; remonstrance chiefs had not.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate and Remonstrance concurrently Reader: since Qingli, censor deputies often held it; remonstrance chiefs had not.

sentences.zh: 紹興十二年春，万俟离以中 丞、羅汝楫以諫議始兼侍讀，自後每除言路，必兼經筵矣。

translations.literal: In spring of the twelfth year of Shaoxing, Wan Qixie as vice censor-in-chief and Luo Ruji as remonstrance adviser were first concurrent Readers-in-Waiting; thereafter every remonstrance appointment included the classics hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 12 spring, Wan Qixie and Luo Ruji were first concurrent Readers; thereafter remonstrance posts included the classics hall.

sentences.zh: 翰林侍講學士

translations.literal: Hanlin Lecturer-in-Waiting Academician
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Lecturer-in-Waiting Academician

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，國子祭酒邢昺為侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, National University Chancellor Xing Bing was Lecturer-in-Waiting academician.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 2, Chancellor Xing Bing was Lecturer-in-Waiting academician.

sentences.zh: 其後，又以馬宗元為侍講，不加別名，但供職而 已。

translations.literal: Later Ma Zongyuan was also Lecturer-in-Waiting without a separate title, merely performing duties.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ma Zongyuan was Lecturer-in-Waiting without separate title, merely performing duties.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，以翰林侍講學士邢昺知曹州，侍講學士外使自昺始。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde, Hanlin Lecturer-in-Waiting Xing Bing was made prefect of Caozhou—the first external assignment of a Lecturer-in-Waiting academician, beginning with Bing.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 4, Xing Bing was made Caozhou prefect—the first external Lecturer-in-Waiting assignment.

sentences.zh: 故事，自兩省、臺 端以上兼侍講，元祐中，司馬康以著作佐郎兼侍講，時朝議以文正公之賢，故特有是命 。

sentences.zh: 乾道六年，張栻始以吏部員外 郎兼。

translations.literal: Zhang Fu in the twenty-fifth year of Shaoxing as chancellor of the university, Wang Zuo in the second year of Longxing as inspection commissioner, and Lin Xian in the seventh year of Qiandao as clan director also entered the classics hall as concurrent Lecturers-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu, Wang Zuo, and Lin Xian also entered as concurrent Lecturers-in-Waiting under special circumstances.

sentences.zh: 蓋扶本以言路兼說書就升其秩， 佐時攝版曹，憲嘗為右史且有舊例，故稍優之。

translations.literal: Fu was promoted from expositor on the remonstrance path; Zuo was acting on the Ministry of Revenue; Xian had been right historian and there was old precedent—thus slightly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Fu rose from expositor via remonstrance; Zuo acted on Revenue; Xian had been right historian with old precedent.

sentences.zh: 宮觀兼侍講：國初自元豐以來，多以宮觀兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Palace abbey concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting: from the founding through Yuanfeng, many palace abbey commissioners were concurrent Readers-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Palace abbey concurrent Lecturer: from the founding through Yuanfeng many abbey commissioners were concurrent Readers.

sentences.zh: 乾道七年，寶文待制胡銓除提舉佑神 觀兼侍講。

sentences.zh: 」故有是命。

sentences.zh: 」時賈昌朝由使相右僕射、觀文殿大學士判尚書都省。

translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of the Hall for Assisting Governance

translations.idiomatic: Assisting Governance lay east of Dragon Diagram Pavilion.
