translations.idiomatic: These were temporary grace grants, not necessarily obtainable.

sentences.zh: 元祐二年，詔復增館職及職事官並許帶職 ，尚待二年加直學士，中丞、侍郎、給捨、諫議通及一年加待制。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanyou an edict restored increased academy posts and allowed active-duty officials to hold concurrent titles; still two years for Direct Academician, one year for vice censor-in-chief, vice minister, drafting, and remonstrance for awaiting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 2 academy posts were restored with concurrent titles; two years for Direct, one year for vice censor, vice minister, drafting, and remonstrance for awaiting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 紹聖三年，詔職事官 罷帶職，非職事之官仍舊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaosheng an edict abolished concurrent titles for active-duty officials; non–active-duty officials remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng 3 active-duty officials lost concurrent titles; others remained.

sentences.zh: 中興後，學士率以授中司、列曹尚書、翰林學士之輔外者， 權尚書、給諫、侍郎則帶直學士、待制焉。

translations.literal: After the restoration, academicians were mostly given to deputy bureau chiefs of the Six Ministries and Hanlin assistants; acting ministers, drafting, remonstrance, and vice ministers received Direct Academician or awaiting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, academicians went to Six Ministry deputies and Hanlin assistants; acting ministers and drafting officials received Direct or awaiting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 龍圖閣學士 直學士 待制

translations.literal: Dragon Diagram Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner
translations.idiomatic: Dragon Diagram Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中建。

translations.literal: Established in the Dazhong Xiangfu era.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Dazhong Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 在會慶殿西偏，北連禁中，閤東曰資政殿，西曰述古殿。

translations.literal: West of Celebratory Assembly Hall, north connecting to the forbidden palace; east of the pavilion was Assisting Governance Hall, west was Pursuing Antiquity Hall.
translations.idiomatic: West of Celebratory Assembly Hall, north to the forbidden palace; east Assisting Governance, west Pursuing Antiquity.

sentences.zh: 閤上以奉太宗 御書、御製文集及典籍、圖畫、寶瑞之物，及宗正寺所進屬籍、世譜。

translations.literal: Above the pavilion were kept Taizong's imperial writings, collected works, classics, paintings, and treasures, and clan registers and genealogies submitted by the Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Above the pavilion were Taizong's writings, classics, paintings, treasures, and clan registers from the Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 有學士、直學 士、待制、直閤等官。

translations.literal: There were academicians, direct academicians, awaiting commissioners, and direct attendants.
translations.idiomatic: There were academicians, direct academicians, awaiting commissioners, and direct attendants.

sentences.zh: 學士，大中祥符三年置，以杜鎬為之，班在樞密直學士上。

translations.literal: Academician: established in the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu with Du Hao appointed, formation above Military Bureau Direct Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Academician: established Dazhong Xiangfu 3 with Du Hao, above Military Bureau Direct Academician.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔結銜在本官之上。

translations.literal: In the sixth year an edict fixed combined title above the original office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year combined title was fixed above the original office.

sentences.zh: 直學士，景德四年置，以杜鎬為之，班在樞密直學士下。

translations.literal: Direct Academician: established in the fourth year of Jingde with Du Hao appointed, formation below Military Bureau Direct Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Academician: Jingde 4 with Du Hao, below Military Bureau Direct.

sentences.zh: 祥符六年，詔結銜在本官之上 。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xiangfu an edict fixed combined title above the original office.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiangfu 6 combined title was fixed above the original office.

sentences.zh: 待制，景德元年置，以杜鎬、戚綸為之，並依舊充職。

translations.literal: Awaiting Commissioner: established in the first year of Jingde with Du Hao and Qi Lun appointed, both continuing former duties.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting Commissioner: Jingde 1 with Du Hao and Qi Lun, continuing former duties.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔班在知制誥下，並赴內 殿起居。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict fixed formation below Drafting Academician, attending inner hall audiences.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year formation was below Drafting Academician with inner hall attendance.

sentences.zh: 自改官制，為學士初復之職，或知制誥平出除之。

translations.literal: Under the reformed official system this was the academician's initial restored post, or conferred on leaving drafting office.
translations.idiomatic: Under the reformed system this was the initial restored academician post, or on leaving drafting.

sentences.zh: 天章閣學士 直學士 待制

translations.literal: Heavenly Writings Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly Writings Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner

sentences.zh: 天禧四年建。

translations.literal: Established in the fourth year of Tianxi.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Tianxi 4.

sentences.zh: 在會慶殿之西，龍圖閣之北。

translations.literal: West of Celebratory Assembly Hall, north of Dragon Diagram Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: West of Celebratory Assembly Hall, north of Dragon Diagram Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 明年，仁宗即位，修天章閣畢，以奉安真宗 御制。

translations.literal: The next year when Renzong took the throne, Heavenly Writings Pavilion was completed to house Zhenzong's imperial compositions.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne, the pavilion was completed for Zhenzong's compositions.

sentences.zh: 東曰群玉殿，西曰蕊，北曰壽昌殿，南曰延康殿。

translations.literal: East was Jade Cluster Hall, west was Pistil Pearl, north Longevity Prosperity, south Extended Health.
translations.idiomatic: East Jade Cluster, west Pistil Pearl, north Longevity Prosperity, south Extended Health.

sentences.zh: 內以桃花文石為流桮之所。

translations.literal: Within, peach-blossom patterned stone was the floating-cup place.
translations.idiomatic: Within, peach-blossom stone was the floating-cup place.

sentences.zh: 以 在位受天書祥符，改曰天章，取為章於天之義。

translations.literal: Because the reign received Heavenly Writings under Xiangfu, it was renamed Heavenly Writings—meaning manifest in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Because the reign received Heavenly Writings under Xiangfu, it was renamed Heavenly Writings—manifest in Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天聖八年置待制。

translations.literal: Awaiting Commissioner established in the eighth year of Tiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting Commissioner established in Tiansheng 8.

sentences.zh: 慶曆七年，又置學士 、直學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qingli, academician and direct academician were also established.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli 7 academician and direct academician were established.

sentences.zh: 又有侍講。

translations.literal: There was also Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 學士，慶曆七年初置，在龍圖閣學士之下。

translations.literal: Academician: first established in the seventh year of Qingli, below Dragon Diagram academician.
translations.idiomatic: Academician: Qingli 7, below Dragon Diagram.

sentences.zh: 學士罕以命人，迄仁 宗世，纔王贄一人。

translations.literal: Academicians were rarely appointed; through Renzong's reign only Wang Zan was one.
translations.idiomatic: Rarely appointed; through Renzong only Wang Zan.

sentences.zh: 秦堪自顯謨閣進直天章閤，以稱呼非便辭。

translations.literal: Qin Kan advanced from Illustrious Exposition to Direct Heavenly Writings Pavilion and declined because the title was inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Kan advanced from Illustrious Exposition to Direct Heavenly Writings and declined as inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 詔改龍圖，自是天章不 為帶職。

translations.literal: An edict changed it to Dragon Diagram; thereafter Heavenly Writings was not a concurrent title.
translations.idiomatic: Changed to Dragon Diagram; Heavenly Writings was no longer concurrent.

sentences.zh: 王曮直學士，慶曆七年，初置天章閣直學士，在龍圖閣直學士之下。

translations.literal: Wang Yan Direct Academician: in the seventh year of Qingli Heavenly Writings Direct Academician was first established, below Dragon Diagram Direct.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan: Qingli 7 Heavenly Writings Direct was established below Dragon Diagram Direct.

sentences.zh: 待制，天 聖八年初置。

translations.literal: Awaiting Commissioner: first established in the eighth year of Tiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting Commissioner: Tiansheng 8.

sentences.zh: 寓直於秘閣，與龍圖遞宿，尋命范諷鞠詠充職。

translations.literal: Resident duty at the Secret Pavilion, alternating night watch with Dragon Diagram; soon Fan Feng and Ju Yong were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Resident duty at Secret Pavilion, alternating with Dragon Diagram; Fan Feng and Ju Yong appointed.

sentences.zh: 中興後，圖籍、符瑞、寶 玩之物，若國史、宗正寺所進屬籍，獨藏於天章閣，祖宗御容、潛邸旌節亦安奉焉。

translations.literal: After the restoration, books, talismans, treasures, national histories, and clan registers were kept only at Heavenly Writings, with ancestral portraits and princely banners also enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, books, talismans, histories, and registers were kept at Heavenly Writings with ancestral portraits.

sentences.zh: 寶文閣學士 直學士 待制

translations.literal: Treasured Literature Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner
translations.idiomatic: Treasured Literature Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner

sentences.zh: 閤在天章閣之東西序，群玉、蕊珠殿之北。

translations.literal: The pavilion lay east and west of Heavenly Writings, north of Jade Cluster and Pistil Pearl halls.
translations.idiomatic: East and west of Heavenly Writings, north of Jade Cluster and Pistil Pearl.

sentences.zh: 即舊壽昌閤，慶曆改曰寶文。

translations.literal: It was the old Longevity Prosperity Pavilion; renamed Treasured Literature in Qingli.
translations.idiomatic: Old Longevity Prosperity; renamed Treasured Literature in Qingli.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐八年，英 宗即位，詔以仁宗御書、御集藏於閤，命王珪撰記立石。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiayou when Yingzong took the throne, an edict housed Renzong's writings in the pavilion; Wang Gui was ordered to compose an inscription and set a stone.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou 8 Yingzong housed Renzong's writings; Wang Gui composed an inscription.

sentences.zh: 治平四年，神宗即位，始置學 士、直學士、待制，恩賜如龍圖。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiping when Shenzong took the throne, academician, direct, and awaiting commissioner were established with favors like Dragon Diagram.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiping 4 Shenzong established posts with Dragon Diagram favors.

sentences.zh: 英宗御書附於閤。

translations.literal: Yingzong's imperial writings were appended to the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong's writings were appended.

sentences.zh: 學士，治平四年初置，以呂公著兼。

translations.literal: Academician: first established in the fourth year of Zhiping with Lü Gongzhu concurrent.
translations.idiomatic: Academician: Zhiping 4 with Lü Gongzhu concurrent.

sentences.zh: 直學士，治平四年初置，以邵必為之。

translations.literal: Direct Academician: first established in the fourth year of Zhiping with Shao Bi appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Direct: Zhiping 4 with Shao Bi.

sentences.zh: 待制，治平四年初置。

translations.literal: Awaiting Commissioner: first established in the fourth year of Zhiping.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting Commissioner: Zhiping 4.

sentences.zh: 顯謨閣學士 直學士 待制

translations.literal: Illustrious Exposition Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner
translations.idiomatic: Illustrious Exposition Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner

sentences.zh: 元符元年，曾布、鄧洵仁各申請建閤。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, Zeng Bu and Deng Xunren each requested establishment of a pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu 1, Zeng Bu and Deng Xunren requested a pavilion.

sentences.zh: 詔翰林學士、中書舍人撰閤名五以聞，遂建閤藏 神宗御集，以顯謨為名。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hanlin academicians and drafting academicians to submit five pavilion names; a pavilion was built to house Shenzong's collected works, named Illustrious Exposition.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin and drafting academicians submitted five names; pavilion housed Shenzong's works as Illustrious Exposition.

sentences.zh: 徽宗建中靖國元年，詔以顯謨閣為熙明閤，仍置學士、直學士 、待制；

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo an edict renamed Illustrious Exposition to Bright Enlightenment and established posts;
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhong Jingguo 1 renamed to Bright Enlightenment with posts;

sentences.zh: 續奉旨，仍以顯謨為額。

translations.literal: by further imperial intent the Illustrious Exposition name was retained.
translations.idiomatic: Illustrious Exposition name was retained.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，詔顯謨閣學士、直學士、待制如三閤故事 ，序位在寶文閤學士、直學士、待制之下。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning an edict fixed Illustrious Exposition posts like the three pavilions, ranking below Treasured Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Chongning 1 fixed posts below Treasured Literature like the three pavilions.

sentences.zh: 學士、直學士、待制，並建中靖國元年置。

translations.literal: Academician, direct, and awaiting commissioner were all established in Jianzhong Jingguo 1.
translations.idiomatic: All established in Jianzhong Jingguo 1.

sentences.zh: 徽猷閣學士 直學士 待制 大觀二年，初建徽猷閣，以藏哲宗御集。

translations.literal: Splendid Virtue Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner. In the second year of Daguan, Splendid Virtue Pavilion was first built to house Zhezong's collected works.
translations.idiomatic: Splendid Virtue Academician; Direct; Awaiting Commissioner. Daguan 2 built for Zhezong's works.

sentences.zh: 置學士、直學士、待制等官。

translations.literal: Academician, direct, and awaiting commissioner posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: Academician, direct, and awaiting commissioner were established.

sentences.zh: 敷文閣學士 直學士 待制 紹興十年置。

translations.literal: Spreading Culture Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner. Established in the tenth year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Spreading Culture Academician; Direct; Awaiting Commissioner. Shaoxing 10.

sentences.zh: 藏徽宗聖制，置學士等官。

translations.literal: It housed Huizong's sacred compositions; academicians and related posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: It housed Huizong's compositions; posts were established.

sentences.zh: 煥章閤學士 直學士 待制 淳熙初建。

translations.literal: Resplendent Seal Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner. Established early in Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: Resplendent Seal Academician; Direct; Awaiting Commissioner. Early Chunxi.

sentences.zh: 藏高宗御制。

translations.literal: It housed Gaozong's imperial compositions.
translations.idiomatic: It housed Gaozong's compositions.

sentences.zh: 十五年，置學士等官。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, academicians and related posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year posts were established.

sentences.zh: 華文閤學士 直學士 待制 慶元二年置。

translations.literal: Flowering Culture Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner. Established in the second year of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Flowering Culture Academician; Direct; Awaiting Commissioner. Qingyuan 2.

sentences.zh: 藏孝宗御制，置學士等官。

translations.literal: It housed Xiaozong's imperial compositions; academicians and related posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: It housed Xiaozong's compositions; posts established.

sentences.zh: 寶謨閤學士 直學士 待制 嘉泰二年置。

translations.literal: Treasured Exposition Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner. Established in the second year of Jiatai.
translations.idiomatic: Treasured Exposition Academician; Direct; Awaiting Commissioner. Jiatai 2.

sentences.zh: 藏光宗御制，置學士等官。

translations.literal: It housed Guangzong's imperial compositions; academicians and related posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: It housed Guangzong's compositions; posts established.

sentences.zh: 寶章閤學士 直學士 待制 寶慶二年置。

translations.literal: Treasured Seal Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner. Established in the second year of Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Treasured Seal Academician; Direct; Awaiting Commissioner. Baoqing 2.

sentences.zh: 藏寧宗御制，置學士等官。

translations.literal: It housed Ningzong's imperial compositions; academicians and related posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: It housed Ningzong's compositions; posts established.

sentences.zh: 顯文閤學士 直學士 待制 咸淳元年置。

translations.literal: Manifest Culture Pavilion Academician; Direct Academician; Awaiting Commissioner. Established in the first year of Xianchun.
translations.idiomatic: Manifest Culture Academician; Direct; Awaiting Commissioner. Xianchun 1.

sentences.zh: 藏理宗御制，置學士等官。

translations.literal: It housed Lizong's imperial compositions; academicians and related posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: It housed Lizong's compositions; posts established.

sentences.zh: 集英殿修撰

translations.literal: Assembled Talent Hall Compiler
translations.idiomatic: Assembled Talent Hall Compiler

sentences.zh: 國初，有集賢殿修撰、直龍圖閣、直秘閣三等。

translations.literal: At the founding there were Assembled Talent Hall compiler, Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion, and Direct Secret Pavilion—three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding: Assembled Talent compiler, Direct Dragon Diagram, Direct Secret Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 政和六年，始置集英殿修撰、右文殿修 撰、秘閣修撰。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenghe, Assembled Talent Hall compiler, Right Culture Hall compiler, and Secret Pavilion compiler were first established.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghe 6 established Assembled Talent, Right Culture, and Secret Pavilion compilers.

sentences.zh: 舊制，貼職無雜壓，至是因增置，乃定為雜壓。

translations.literal: Concurrent titles had no mixed precedence; with the additions precedence was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent titles had no mixed precedence; additions fixed it.

sentences.zh: 其集英修撰，中興後以 寵六曹權侍郎之補外者，下待制一等。

translations.literal: Assembled Talent compiler after the restoration honored acting vice ministers of the Six Ministries assigned outside, one rank below awaiting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration Assembled Talent compiler honored acting vice ministers outside, below awaiting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 右文殿修撰

translations.literal: Right Culture Hall Compiler
translations.idiomatic: Right Culture Hall Compiler

sentences.zh: 元佑元年，許內外官帶貼職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, inner and outer officials were permitted concurrent registry titles.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou 1 permitted concurrent registry titles.

sentences.zh: 紹聖二年，詔職事官罷帶職，易集賢殿學士為修撰。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaosheng an edict abolished concurrent titles for active-duty officials; Assembled Talent academician was changed to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Shaosheng 2 abolished active-duty concurrent titles; Assembled Talent academician became compiler.

sentences.zh: 政和 六年，以集賢院無此名，其見任集賢院修撰並改為右文殿修撰，次於集英殿修撰，為貼 職之高等。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenghe, because Assembled Talent had no such name, incumbent compilers were changed to Right Culture compilers, below Assembled Talent, the high rank of registry titles.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghe 6 renamed to Right Culture compiler below Assembled Talent.

sentences.zh: 秘閣修撰 政和六年置，以待館閣之資深者，仍多由直龍圖閤遷焉。

translations.literal: Secret Pavilion Compiler: established Zhenghe 6 for senior academy staff, often promoted from Direct Dragon Diagram.
translations.idiomatic: Secret Pavilion Compiler: Zhenghe 6 for senior academy staff, often from Direct Dragon Diagram.

sentences.zh: 直龍圖閣

translations.literal: Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion
translations.idiomatic: Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion

sentences.zh: 祥符九年，以馮元為太子中允、直龍圖閣，直閤之名始此。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xiangfu, Feng Yuan was made Crown Prince Vice Commissioner and Direct Dragon Diagram—the origin of Direct Attendant title.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangfu 9 Feng Yuan was Direct Dragon Diagram—origin of Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 凡館閣之久次者，必選直龍 圖閣，皆為擢待制之基也。

translations.literal: Those long in the academy were always selected as Direct Dragon Diagram, the basis for promotion to awaiting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Long academy service led to Direct Dragon Diagram, basis for awaiting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 中興後，凡直閤為庶官任藩閫、監司者貼職，各隨高下而等 差之。

translations.literal: After the restoration, Direct Attendant as registry for lower officials in provinces and transit followed rank in gradation.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration Direct Attendant registry for provincial officials followed rank.

sentences.zh: 直天章閣至直顯文閤並同。

translations.literal: Direct Heavenly Writings through Direct Manifest Culture were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Heavenly Writings through Direct Manifest Culture were the same.

sentences.zh: 東宮官 太子太師 太傅 太保 太子少師 少傅 少保

translations.literal: Eastern Palace offices: Grand Tutor, Grand Mentor, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; Junior Tutor, Junior Mentor, Junior Guardian
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Palace: Grand Tutor, Mentor, Guardian; Junior Tutor, Mentor, Guardian

sentences.zh: 國初，師傅不常設。

translations.literal: At the founding, tutors and mentors were not regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding tutors were not regularly established.

sentences.zh: 仁宗升儲，置三少各一人。

translations.literal: When Renzong was made heir, three juniors were each established one.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was heir, three juniors were established.

sentences.zh: 參政李昉兼掌賓客。

translations.literal: Participating executive Li Fang concurrently directed palace guests.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang concurrently directed palace guests.

sentences.zh: 及升首相，遂進少 傅，此宰相兼宮僚之始也。

translations.literal: On promotion to chief minister he advanced to Junior Mentor—the beginning of grand councillors as palace officials.
translations.idiomatic: On becoming chief minister he became Junior Mentor—grand councillors as palace officials began.

sentences.zh: 丁謂兼少師，馮拯兼少傅，曹利用兼少保，是時實為東宮官 ，餘多以前宰執為致仕官。

translations.literal: Ding Wei as Junior Tutor, Feng Zheng as Junior Mentor, Cao Liyong as Junior Guardian—then truly Eastern Palace offices; most others were former chancellors in retirement posts.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei, Feng Zheng, and Cao Liyong were true palace offices; others were retired chancellors.

sentences.zh: 若太子太師、太傅、太保，以待宰相官未至僕射者，及樞密 使致仕，亦隨本官高下除授。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor, Mentor, and Guardian awaited grand councillors not yet Vice Directors and military commissioners in retirement, appointed by original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Grand posts awaited grand councillors not yet Vice Directors and retired military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 太子少師、少傅、少保，以待前執政，惟少師非經顧命不 除。

translations.literal: Junior Tutor, Mentor, and Guardian awaited former executives; only Junior Tutor was not conferred without testamentary appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Junior posts awaited former executives; Junior Tutor required testamentary appointment.

sentences.zh: 若因遷轉，則遞進一官，至太師即遷司空。

translations.literal: On transfer, one rank advanced in succession; at Grand Tutor one advanced to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On transfer one rank advanced; at Grand Tutor one became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 天禧末，皇太子同聽政，乃以首相兼少 師。

translations.literal: At the end of Tiansheng the heir apparent jointly heard government; the chief minister was made concurrent Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: At Tiansheng end the heir heard government; chief minister was concurrent Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 自後神宗、欽宗、孝宗、光宗在東宮，皆不置。

translations.literal: Thereafter when Shenzong, Qinzong, Xiaozong, and Guangzong were heirs, none were established.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter for Shenzong, Qinzong, Xiaozong, and Guangzong as heirs, none were established.

sentences.zh: 開禧三年，史彌遠自詹事入樞府， 乃進兼賓客。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaixi, Shi Miyuan from palace director entered the Military Bureau and was advanced to concurrent palace guest.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaixi 3, Shi Miyuan from palace director entered the Military Bureau and became concurrent palace guest.

sentences.zh: 已而太子侍立，遂以丞相錢象祖兼太子少傅。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent attended, Grand Councillor Qian Xiangzu was made concurrent Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir attended, Qian Xiangzu was concurrent Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 明年，景獻太子立，象祖兼 少師，彌遠以右相兼少傅。

translations.literal: The next year Prince Jingxian was established; Xiangzu was concurrent Junior Tutor and Miyuan as right grand councillor concurrent Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingxian was established; Xiangzu Junior Tutor, Miyuan Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，彌遠丁內艱，像祖亦去位。

translations.literal: Before long Miyuan mourned his mother and Xiangzu also left office.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan mourned; Xiangzu left office.

sentences.zh: 又明年，彌遠起復，遂兼 進少師。

translations.literal: The next year Miyuan resumed office and was advanced to concurrent Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Miyuan resumed and became concurrent Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 景定元年，度宗升儲，以賈似道為少師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingding, when Duzong was made heir, Jia Sidao was Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingding 1, Duzong as heir, Jia Sidao Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 太子賓客

translations.literal: Palace Guest of the Heir Apparent
translations.idiomatic: Palace Guest of the Heir Apparent

sentences.zh: 至道元年建儲，初置賓客二人，以他官兼。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao when the heir was established, two guests were first appointed, filled by other officials concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidao 1 two guests were appointed, filled concurrently.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年，參政任中正、樞副錢惟演、參政 王曾並兼太子賓客，執政兼東宮官始此。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiansheng, participating executive Ren Zhongzheng, vice military commissioner Qian Weiyan, and participating executive Wang Zeng were all concurrent palace guests—the beginning of executives as Eastern Palace officials.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng 4 Ren Zhongzheng, Qian Weiyan, and Wang Zeng were concurrent guests—executives as palace officials began.

sentences.zh: 中興後不置。

translations.literal: After the restoration it was not established.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration it was not established.

sentences.zh: 開禧三年，景獻太子立，始以執 政兼賓客，後復省。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaixi when Prince Jingxian was established, executives were first made concurrent guests; later abolished again.
translations.idiomatic: Kaixi 3 Prince Jingxian: executives concurrent guests; later abolished.

sentences.zh: 景定元年，度宗升儲，以朱熠、皮龍榮、沈炎並兼賓客。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingding when Duzong was made heir, Zhu Yi, Pi Longrong, and Shen Yan were concurrent guests.
translations.idiomatic: Jingding 1 Zhu Yi, Pi Longrong, and Shen Yan were concurrent guests.

translations.idiomatic: Director of the Eastern Palace

translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Subordinates; Left and Right Moral Instructors

translations.literal: Under the old system not regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system not regularly established.

translations.literal: When the heir's residence was built, offices were created as needed with many filled concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir's residence was built, offices were created as needed, often concurrent.

translations.idiomatic: Renzong and Shenzong as heirs: two subordinates and two instructors each.

translations.idiomatic: Qinzong as heir: one of each.

translations.idiomatic: Palace lecturing has no precedent; follow classics hall with reduced ritual.

translations.literal: The heir apparent sits in the main seat; reading officers rise in turn as at Yanying and return after lecture.
translations.idiomatic: The heir sits main seat; readers rise as at Yanying and return.

translations.idiomatic: On festivals palace officials do not receive congratulations;

translations.idiomatic: on New Year and winter solstice the director and below submit felicitations.

sentences.zh: 謝 辭，初如常見之禮。

translations.literal: For thanks and leave, initially like ordinary audience ritual.
translations.idiomatic: For thanks and leave, initially ordinary audience.

translations.literal: Later leaving position to speak, returning to seat, tea ended.
translations.idiomatic: Later leaving position to speak, returning, tea ended.

translations.literal: On the director's first attendance, audience with the heir apparent: bow, heir returns bow.
translations.idiomatic: Director's first attendance: bow, heir returns bow.

translations.literal: Subordinates and others on first attendance: audience, heir receives bow.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates on first attendance: heir receives bow.

sentences.zh: 庶子、諭德及講讀官雖有坐受之禮，止是 五禮新儀所載；

translations.literal: Though subordinates, instructors, and reading officers had seated reception in the Five Rites, daily bows were not practiced;
translations.idiomatic: Seated reception was in Five Rites but daily bows were not practiced;

sentences.zh: 兼逐日致拜之禮，近例皆已不行，或遇合致拜日，更合參酌天禧、至道 故事施行。」

translations.idiomatic: (Tiansheng 2.9.5 Zhang Shisun said: "We attend at Venerating Goodness, ascend and bow then kneel—we hope the heir may sit to receive audience."

translations.idiomatic: Zhidao 1 the heir bowed first to the guest; on seeing off descended to the gate.)

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Central and Regular Attendants
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Central and Regular Attendants

translations.literal: One each established in Zhidao and Tiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: One each in Zhidao and Tiansheng.

translations.literal: When Shenzong and Qinzong were made heirs, established as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong and Qinzong as heirs: as before.

sentences.zh: 嘉定初，除二人。

translations.literal: Early in Jiading, two were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jiading: two appointed.

translations.literal: In Qingyuan the central attendant ranked above the regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingyuan central ranked above regular.

translations.literal: Hall for Venerating Goodness: Companion; Praise Reader; Direct Expositor; Expositor; Primary School Professor of the Eastern Palace; Primary School Professor of the Hall for Venerating Goodness
translations.idiomatic: Hall for Venerating Goodness: Companion; Praise Reader; Direct Expositor; Expositor; Eastern Palace and Venerating Goodness primary professors

translations.literal: Companion, Praise Reader, and Direct Expositor were old institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Companion, Praise Reader, and Direct Expositor were old institutions.

translations.literal: Expositor and below were added after the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Expositor and below were added after the restoration.

translations.literal: The Hall for Venerating Goodness when Renzong was prince was the place of study; when princes went to external tutors, officials were chosen to hold it concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Venerating Goodness when Renzong was prince was for study; external tutors held it concurrently.

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanfeng when Zhezong first opened the classics lecture, reading officers attended daily on alternate days with one on night duty.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfeng 8 Zhezong opened lecture: officers attended on alternate days with night duty.

sentences.zh: 又詔三省、樞密院、講讀 、修注官錫宴於資善堂。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Three Departments, Military Bureau, reading and revising officers to a feast at Venerating Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Three Departments, Military Bureau, and reading officers feasted at Venerating Goodness.

sentences.zh: 政和元年，定王、嘉王出就資善堂聽讀，詔宰執就見。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenghe, Princes Ding and Jia attended at Venerating Goodness; an edict ordered chief ministers to attend audience.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghe 1 Princes Ding and Jia attended; chief ministers received audience.

sentences.zh: 靖康元 年，詔皇太子出就外傅，就資善堂置學舍，令國子監供監書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang an edict ordered the heir to external tutors, school quarters at Venerating Goodness, and the National University to supply texts.
translations.idiomatic: Jingkang 1 heir to external tutors; Venerating Goodness school; National University supplied texts.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，孝宗封建國公 ，出就資善堂聽講。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing, Xiaozong as Prince of Jian attended lectures at Venerating Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 5 Xiaozong as Prince of Jian attended at Venerating Goodness.

sentences.zh: 先是，宰臣趙鼎得旨於宮門內造書院，至是始成，以為資善堂。

translations.literal: Earlier Grand Councillor Zhao Ding had built a academy within the palace gate; now completed as Venerating Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding had built an academy; now completed as Venerating Goodness.

sentences.zh: 命 儒臣為直講、翊善，悉如資善故事。

translations.literal: Confucian officials as Direct Expositor and Companion followed Venerating Goodness precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian Direct Expositor and Companion followed precedent.

sentences.zh: 尋用趙鼎言，以左史范沖充翊善，右史朱震充贊讀 ，時稱極選。

translations.idiomatic: Fan Chong Companion and Zhu Zhen Praise Reader—supreme selection.

translations.idiomatic: The emperor said the state prince must bow to Chong and Zhen out of respect for teachers.

sentences.zh: 」紹興十 二年，建國公出就外第。

translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 12 the state prince moved out.

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Shaoxing, from Prince of Pu'an to prince, advanced to Prince of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 30 from Pu'an to prince, advanced to Jian.

translations.idiomatic: Imperial grandsons studied with Wang Shipeng as primary professor.

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Shaoxing when Xiaozong took the throne, one expositor each for the three princes' ranks, plus Praise Reader and Direct Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 32 one expositor per prince rank plus Praise Reader and Direct Expositor.

sentences.zh: 淳熙七年，皇孫英國公始就傅，詔置皇太子宮小學教授一員。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chunxi when imperial grandson Prince of England first studied, one Eastern Palace primary professor was established.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 7 Prince of England: one Eastern Palace primary professor.

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year when Guangzong took the throne, the prince advanced to Prince of Jia with one each of Praise Reader, Companion, and Direct Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: Year 16 prince became Jia with Praise Reader, Companion, and Direct Expositor.

translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan 6 Prince Jingxian: Venerating Goodness with two primary professors.

translations.literal: Imperial nephews and grandsons had tutoring and north-south companion readers without fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial nephews and grandsons had tutors and companion readers without fixed number.

sentences.zh: （至道初，太宗以 皇親子孫就講學，欲置侍講之職，中書言：「按唐太宗改諸王侍讀為奉諸王講讀，今皇 孫、皇姪皆環衛之職，請以教授為名。

translations.literal: (Early Zhidao Taizong had imperial sons and grandsons study and wished to establish lecturing; the Secretariat said: "Tang Taizong changed princes' readers to instructors for princes; now imperial grandsons and nephews are guard posts—please name them professors."
translations.idiomatic: (Zhidao Taizong wished lecturing; Secretariat said use professor for grandsons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 選京朝官通經者充。

translations.literal: Capital officials versed in classics were selected.
translations.idiomatic: Capital classicists were selected.

sentences.zh: 其後又令王府記室 、翊善、侍講分兼南北宅教授。

translations.literal: Later princely record, companion, and lecturing officers jointly held north-south residence professorships.
translations.idiomatic: Later record, companion, and lecturer held north-south professorships.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，又有侍教之名，自是南北院或有伴讀。）〉

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu the tutoring name appeared; thereafter north-south courts sometimes had companion readers.)
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong Xiangfu 2 tutoring appeared; north-south courts sometimes had companion readers.)

sentences.zh: 凡諸宮皆有教授，初無定員。

translations.literal: Every palace had professors; initially no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Every palace had professors without fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 是年，英宗以宗室自率府副率已上八百餘人，奉朝請者 四百餘人，而教官纔六員，乃詔增置教授官：凡皇族年三十已上者百一十三人，置講書 四員；

translations.literal: That year Yingzong said clan from rate vice commander and above numbered over eight hundred, over four hundred court attendees, but only six instructors—an edict increased professors: 113 clan thirty and above, four lecturers;
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong said over eight hundred clan, six instructors—edict increased: 113 age thirty and above, four lecturers;

sentences.zh: 年二十以上者百十三人，置講書四員；

translations.literal: 113 age twenty and above, four lecturers;
translations.idiomatic: 113 age twenty and above, four lecturers;

sentences.zh: 年十五已上者三百九人，增置教授五員；

translations.literal: 309 age fifteen and above, five professors added;
translations.idiomatic: 309 age fifteen and above, five professors;

sentences.zh: 年十四已下者，別置小學教授十二員；

translations.literal: under fourteen, twelve primary school professors;
translations.idiomatic: under fourteen, twelve primary professors;

sentences.zh: 并舊六，為二十七員，以分教之。

translations.literal: with the old six, twenty-seven total to teach separately.
translations.idiomatic: with six old, twenty-seven total.

sentences.zh: 其子弟不率教 ，俾教授官、本位尊長具名申大宗正司，量行戒責。

translations.literal: Disobedient sons were reported by professors and clan elders to the Great Clan Court for discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Disobedient sons were reported to the Great Clan Court for discipline.

sentences.zh: 教授官不職，大宗正司密訪以聞。

translations.literal: Negligent professors were secretly investigated by the Great Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Negligent professors were secretly investigated.

sentences.zh: 舊制，親賢宅置講書，紹興十二年，改為府教授，掌教親賢宅南班宗子。

translations.literal: Under old practice the Noble and Worthy Residence had lecturers; in the twelfth year of Shaoxing changed to establishment professors teaching south-wing clan sons.
translations.idiomatic: Old practice Noble Residence lecturers; Shaoxing 12 establishment professors for south-wing clan.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十二年， 詔建魏惠憲王府，置小學教授二員，以館職兼充，掌訓皇孫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chunxi an edict built Prince Hui of Wei's establishment with two primary professors by academy post, teaching imperial grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 12 Prince Hui establishment: two primary professors from academy.

sentences.zh: 既長，趨朝謁，則不以小 學名，而講習如故。

translations.literal: When grown they attended court audience without primary school name but study continued.
translations.idiomatic: When grown they attended court without primary school name but study continued.

sentences.zh: 自後皇姪、皇孫皆置教授。

translations.literal: Thereafter imperial nephews and grandsons all had professors.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter imperial nephews and grandsons all had professors.
